title: Microscopic magnetic phase evolution in the Weyl semimetal Mn$_3$Sn revealed by $μ^+$SR
authors: U. Miniotaite, O. K. Forslund, H. Luetkens, V. Rai, J. Persson, G. D. Morris, D. Zuhair, D. W. Tam, S. Nandi, Y. Sassa, M. Månsson
abstract: We report a comprehensive muon spin relaxation ($μ^+$SR) and bulk magnetization study of the antiferromagnetic (AFM) Weyl semimetal Mn$_3$Sn (composition Mn$_{2.99}$Sn). Mn$_3$Sn is reported to exhibit a commensurate inverse triangular (IT) AFM phase, an incommensurate (IC) helical AFM phase, and a proposed low-temperature spin-glass-like state. In our sample, we establish the respective transition temperatures for these phases to be $T_\mathrm{N} = 418$ K, $T_\mathrm{t} \approx 275$ K, and $T_\mathrm{f} = 21$ K. Investigating the low-temperature regime below $T_\mathrm{f}$, we find no evidence of a static spin-glass state. Instead, the sample exhibits an increasing ferromagnetic (FM) component accompanied by a localized slowing of spin fluctuations, indicating that these phenomena may be decoupled. In the IC helical AFM phase, fitting the zero-field (ZF) spectra reveals an asymmetric internal magnetic-field distribution, indicating that the magnetic structure is heavily modified by anharmonicity. Upon warming above 150 K, a continuous redistribution of muon spectral weight reveals a broad regime of coexisting local magnetic environments associated with the IC helical and IT-AFM phases. In the commensurate IT-AFM phase above $T_\mathrm{t}$, a persistent missing fraction in the initial asymmetry indicates that a subset of implanted muons, corresponding to roughly 20% of the sample-related asymmetry, undergoes unresolved ultrafast depolarization. Finally, we observe temperature-driven shifts in muon site populations above 325 K. Ultimately, our results show a highly dynamic magnetic landscape in Mn$_3$Sn, demonstrating how its complex magnetic orders often coexist and evolve continuously with temperature.
summary: This work investigates the intricate temperature-dependent magnetic phase evolution in the Weyl semimetal Mn3Sn using muon spin relaxation ($\mu^+$SR) and magnetization measurements. It identifies three distinct magnetic transitions, demonstrating that the material's magnetic state is highly dynamic, featuring coexisting local environments rather than simple sequential ordering. The findings provide detailed microscopic insight into complex magnetism in topological materials.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the microscopic magnetic phase evolution of the Weyl semimetal Mn3Sn across multiple temperature regimes.
main_result: The material exhibits a highly dynamic magnetic landscape characterized by coexisting and continuously evolving complex magnetic orders (IT-AFM, IC-helical) rather than abrupt transitions. The low-temperature state shows an increasing ferromagnetic component decoupled from static spin-glass freezing.
method: Muon Spin Relaxation ($\mu^+$SR) measurements in both Zero-Field (ZF) and Transverse Field (TF), complemented by bulk magnetization ($M(H)$) and AC susceptibility studies.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Weyl semimetal Mn3Sn. The analysis probes its magnetic transitions between an Inverse Triangular Antiferromagnetic (IT-AFM) phase, an Incommensurate Helical Antiferromagnetic (IC-helical) phase, and a low-temperature ferromagnetic component.
key_observables: Muon spin relaxation spectra asymmetry ($A_{	ext{tot}}$), relaxation rates ($\lambda$), bulk magnetization $M(T)$ and $M(H)$, and transition temperatures ($T_N=418 	ext{ K}, T_t \approx 275 	ext{ K}, T_f = 21 	ext{ K}$).
important_parameters: Temperature (ranging from 5 K to 475 K), applied magnetic field, and the fractional loss of initial asymmetry ($\sim 20\%$) in the IT-AFM phase.
main_assumptions: The interpretation of missing muon asymmetry is tentative, suggesting possible origins like domain walls or grain boundaries; further single-crystal measurements are needed for confirmation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic phase diagram showing three transitions. Magnetization curves show hysteresis changes across temperatures, and $\mu^+$SR spectra detail the temperature dependence of oscillations and relaxation rates in different phases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes magnetic behavior using $\mu^+$SR (ZF/TF) to map out multiple magnetic transitions ($T_N, T_t, T_f$). It details the spectral signatures unique to each phase—from IC-helical field distributions to IT-AFM depolarization—culminating in a conclusion of continuous magnetic evolution.
why_interesting: The study uses highly sensitive local probes ($\mu^+$SR) to map out complex, coexisting magnetic orders in a topological material. The observation of continuously evolving phases rather than sharp transitions is relevant for understanding quantum critical points and emergent many-body dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Magnetic phase diagram of Mn3Sn. The evolution of magnetic states is shown as a function of temperature, indicating key transition temperatures (Tf, Tt, and TN). Exact values are omitted here because transition temperatures vary between samples. The spin configurations of the Mn atoms on the kagome lattice are illustrated for the helical antiferromagnetic (AFM) and inverse triangular AFM (IT-AFM) phases. Blue and pink atoms denote Mn atoms located in different layers in the unit cell. Green arrows show the IC spin rotation in subsequent unit cells for the respective layers.
Fig. 2(c) shows the real part of the ACMS of Mn3Sn between 5 K and 80 K. A distinct peak is observed at Tf = 21 K. Notably, our results do not show a frequency- dependent shift for this peak.

FIG. 2: Bulk magnetic characterization. a) Tempera- ture dependence of the magnetization using zero-field-cooled (ZFC) and field-cooled (FC) protocols with an applied mag- netic field of B = 0.1 T, marking key transition temperatures (Tf, Tim, and Tt). b) M(H) curves showing magnetization as a function of applied magnetic field between -5 T and 5 T at 5 K, 20 K, 50 K, and 150 K. The inset provides a magni- fied view of the low-field region to highlight the temperature evolution of the hysteresis. c) Real part of the AC magnetic susceptibility (ACMS), χ′, as a function of temperature across various frequencies, showing a peak near Tf.

FIG. 3: N´eel temperature from TF-µ+SR. (a) Muon spin relaxation (µ+SR) spectra of Mn3Sn measured in an applied transverse field (TF) of B = 50 G at various temperatures. Solid black lines show fits to the experimental data using Eq. (1). (b) Evolution of the fitted TF asymmetry coefficient, A0, as a function of temperature. The sharp magnetic transition is fitted with a sigmoid function (red curve), extracting a N´eel temperature of TN = 418 K.

FIG. 4: Temperature evolution of ZF-µ+SR spectra. Zero-field (ZF) muon spin relaxation (µ+SR) asymmetry of Mn3Sn measured at various temperatures from 5 K to 450 K. Solid black lines show fits to the experimental data using Eq. (2). Successive spectra are vertically offset by a constant value for clarity of presentation.
